items.title: Award-Winning AI Literature
items.summary: Article URL: https://jamesyu.org/award-winning-ai-literature/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50199232 Points: 38 # Comments: 24
items.content:
This a list of literary awards granted to works where AI was used (or was suspected) as part of the writing process

🇯🇵 Short story Are You There? by Kamome Ashizawa — 9th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2022 Ashizawa made 101 stories in three weeks with AI. The story that won was mostly written by Ashizawa with a little AI; the other hundred experiments were mostly machine-generated. This was the first AI-assisted story to win a Hoshi prize.

🇯🇵 Short story The Last Painter by Toh Katagiri — 12th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2025 The organizers classified it as AI-assisted, but never said exactly how. A fellow finalist says Katagiri told the group that every sentence was written personally.

🇯🇵 Short story Genome Tower by Shamizui — 13th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Grand Prix, 2026 The disclosed AI use was apparently limited to inventing the name of a fictional disease. The organizers still counted it among the year’s AI-assisted winners.

🇯🇵 Short story Parallel Self-Mediation Co., Ltd. by En Shijima — 13th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2026 Shijima described working with AI as feeling more like “choosing” than “writing.” This sounds like a much more generative collaboration than Genome Tower . The prize stood.

🇯🇵 Short story Erinnerung by Rino Takinouchi — 13th Nikkei Hoshi Shinichi Literary Award, Excellence Award, 2026 ChatGPT produced initial material. Takinouchi corrected confused pronouns, dated phrases, and broken logic, then changed the title and ending and added the CRISPR-Cas9 material. Of the 2026 Hoshi winners, this has the clearest public account of AI-generated prose being extensively rewritten.

The 13th Hoshi award received 2,107 entries. Organizers counted 491 as partly AI-created and said three of the four general-division winners had used AI somewhere in the process.

🇺🇸 Artist books The Library of Nonhuman Books by Karen Ann Donnachie and Andy Simionato — Robert Coover Award, First Place, 2020 An AI reading machine uses computer vision, OCR, and language processing to find short poetic combinations in physical books, erase the surrounding words, pair them with images, and publish new volumes. One of those volumes, Perception , also won Australia’s Cornish Family Prize.

🇸🇰 Poetry collection Výsledky vzniku by Liza Gennart — Zlatá vlna, 2021 Zuzana Husárová and Ľubomír Panák trained GPT-2 on 2,108 Slovak works, then curated and lightly edited its poems. The collection won Slovakia’s annual prize for the best original Slovak poetry book.

🇺🇸 Poetry series ReRites by David Jhave Johnston — Electronic Literature Organization Robert Coover Award, 2022 Twelve books of poetry built from neural-network output selected and edited by Johnston. The project openly calls itself “Human + A.I. poetry,” which is exactly the kind of thing an electronic-literature award exists to recognize.

🇺🇸 Chapbook A Black Story May Contain Sensitive Content by Lillian-Yvonne Bertram — DIAGRAM/New Michigan Press Chapbook Contest, Winner, 2023 Bertram used GPT-3 and Warpland, a model trained on Gwendolyn Brooks. Three sections contain machine responses to her prompts. The press knew how the book was made and published it openly.

🇺🇸 Short story Stargazers by Ruei-Jie Chang — UCSB Mind & Machine Intelligence Writing Contest, First Prize, 2024 Chang used ChatGPT for the seed of the story and Claude to organize and translate a Mandarin-English draft, then revised it. The contest explicitly welcomed human-only, machine-only, and hybrid entries, and required everyone to document the process.

🇷🇺 Short story 30–70 by Yana Vagner — Valentin Kataev Literary Prize, Winner, 2025 Vagner wrote the story with Alice, Yandex’s AI assistant. It begins by showing her prompt and the AI’s response, then uses the system for recurring climate reports. The collaboration was visible when the story won.

🇬🇧 Generative poem WORDS BEYOND WORDS by Sasha Stiles — Lumen Prize Literature & Poetry Award, 2025 A fine-tuned language model uses Stiles’s prompts, source texts, and code to make a new poem whenever the work is refreshed. The system itself, rather than a single fixed output, received the award.

🇬🇧 Interactive fiction Flesh & Blood by Chris Joseph — Electronic Literature Organization Robert Coover Award, 2026 An interactive story where readers solve puzzles in a disturbing world of bodies and machinery. Joseph openly lists it among his AI-assisted works .

🇫🇷 Novel C’était ça ou mourir by Thélyson Orélien — Prix du Roman Fnac, 2026 The novel won Fnac’s prize, then was removed from the Goncourt longlist after AI allegations. On October 21, Boréal dropped Orélien after an external review reportedly found AI markers in working-document metadata. The publisher said it still did not know how much AI had been used. Orélien had denied that any sentence was machine-generated.

🇸🇬 Poems Migrant Writers of Singapore poetry competition — Migrant Literature Festival, 2024 Eight winners were announced, then the entire list was recalled after organizers said three winning entries were AI-generated. Their review relied partly on Scribbr and QuillBot.

🇺🇸 Poems Poetry.com November and December contests — Two Monthly First Prizes, 2024 Poetry.com said both original winners were created “with assistance” from AI, changed the results, and redistributed the prizes. The removed poems and writers are no longer reliably identifiable. The names on the current result pages are the replacements, not the accused entrants.

🇯🇵 Novel Sympathy Tower Tokyo by Rie Kudan — 170th Akutagawa Prize, 2024 Kudan first guessed that about 5% of the novel involved ChatGPT, then gave a much smaller figure: about one page out of 143. She consulted its output for the replies written by the AI inside the novel. The prize stood.

🇨🇳 Short story The Land of Machine Memories by Shen Yang, writing as “QuartZen” — 5th Youth Popular Science and Science Fiction Competition, Second Prize, 2023 AI generated the title, prose, illustrations, and pen name over 66 rounds of prompting. The organizer invited Shen and hid the experiment from the judges. This is often called a national literary prize, but it was a broad Jiangsu association contest: 18 stories shared second prize and 90 of roughly 200 entries received awards.

🇯🇵 Web novel Modest Skill “Tidying Up” Is the Strongest! — 18th AlphaPolis Fantasy Novel Awards, Grand Prize and Reader’s Choice, 2025 The author said a large majority of the web novel was made with generative AI. AlphaPolis later canceled the print edition and manga adaptation and changed its rules. Reporting confirms those cancellations, but not that the two award labels were formally revoked.

🇺🇸 Memoir How to Win One Million Dollars and $#!T Glitter! by Luke Stoffel — IBPA Book Award, Benjamin Franklin Silver Medal for Neurodivergent Communities, 2026 Stoffel says he used ChatGPT for grammar and structural scaffolding and disclosed it in the book and award submission. IBPA’s guidelines did not prohibit AI-assisted work , and the book received Silver. IBPA has not publicly commented on his AI use.

🇿🇼 Short story The Blue Fighter by Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza — Caine Prize for African Writing, Winner, 2026 Pangram flagged almost the entire story as AI-generated, according to The Atlantic . Kundizeza denied using AI and said the story drew on his family’s experiences. The prize opened a review. No final finding or revocation had been announced as of October 21.

🇬🇧 Short story The Serpent in the Grove by Jamir Nazir — Commonwealth Short Story Prize, Overall Winner, 2026 Pangram called it 100% AI-generated. Nazir denied it and described six or seven drafts made with Android speech-to-text because of a chronic condition. The Commonwealth Foundation reviewed drafts, timestamps, notes, and testimony, accepted his account, and kept the award. The allegation is disputed, not proven.

🇬🇧 Short story The Bastion’s Shadow by John Edward DeMicoli — Commonwealth Short Story Prize, Canada and Europe Winner, 2026 Pangram also returned 100% here. DeMicoli produced handwritten drafts, notes, and years of research and denied using AI. The Foundation accepted the evidence and the prize stood.

🇬🇧 Short story Mehendi Nights by Sharon Aruparayil — Commonwealth Short Story Prize, Asia Winner, 2026 Aruparayil denied using AI at any stage and kept a paper trail. She also found that adding three Marathi words and removing one word made a flagged section register as 100% human. The Foundation kept the award.

🇬🇧 Short story Descend by Chanel Sutherland — Commonwealth Short Story Prize, Overall Winner, 2025 Pangram scanned the story a year later and labeled it 88% AI-generated. Sutherland denied using AI and said its repetition and rhythm come from Vincentian oral storytelling. Her publisher and agent backed her. No public provenance review of the 2025 story has been released.

🇬🇧 Short story Back and Forth by Kavyta Kay — Harper’s Bazaar UK Short Story Competition, Winner, 2026 A screenshot of a 100% Pangram result spread online. No author response, organizer investigation, admission, or revocation has surfaced.

items.title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax
items.summary: The Meta boss had said he would exit the state over a wealth tax that has not yet come into force.
items.content:
Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.

The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.

The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn. It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.

He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.

California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.

The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years. Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in California was less than 1% , external each year.

Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state. His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.

Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.

It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.

In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.

Through what's known as a stock split announced by the company on Wednesday , Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder. Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.

Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing. The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.

The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.

Meta called the deal with Zuckerberg its "Founder Alignment Agreement," saying it was "critically important" to keep him leading the company from California given the "dramatic and unprecedented transformation taking place in the tech industry and global economy related to artificial intelligence."

The company alluded to problems the company experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Zuckerberg began working outside of the office and mostly from his large compound in Kauai, Hawaii.

After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.

Layoffs have continued into this year. The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.

Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.

With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.

Major tech companies are set to spend an estimated $1 trillion , external this year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, like data centres .

Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects. The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.

It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago. Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.

And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead. Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.

The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.

Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.

items.title: Un Monet venduto per 50 milioni di euro a Parigi, record all'asta
items.summary: Il dipinto 'Iris' presentato al pubblico per la prima volta
items.content:
"Iris", un'opera monumentale dipinta da Claude Monet verso la fine della sua vita, è stata battuta all'asta a Parigi per 50 milioni di euro (commissioni incluse), diventando l'opera d'arte più costosa mai venduta all'asta in Francia, secondo la casa d'aste Sotheby's. Il dipinto del maestro dell'impressionismo veniva presentato al pubblico per la prima volta. Prima della vendita, la sua stima oscillava tra i 22 e i 30 milioni di euro. L'opera di grandi dimensioni (1,60 metri di altezza per 1,80 metri di larghezza) non aveva mai lasciato la residenza parigina della famiglia Schlumberger.

Secondo Thomas Bompard, codirettore del dipartimento di arte moderna e contemporanea di Sotheby's Francia, il quadro era stato acquistato dalla famiglia del pittore da Jeanne Schlumberger (1889-1983), "una brillante collezionista d'arte". "Iris" era stato valutato tra i 22 e i 30 milioni di euro, ovvero "la stima più alta mai attribuita a un dipinto presentato a un'asta in Francia", come aveva indicato Sotheby's durante la presentazione della vendita a settembre. Tre dipinti di Paul Cézanne, classificati come "tesori nazionali", sono stati inoltre ritirati dalla vendita poche ore prima dell'inizio dell'asta, "nell'ottica di un loro ritorno nella città natale dell'artista, Aix-en-Provence", fa sapere Sotheby's. Tale ritorno è il risultato di un'intesa "tra gli attuali proprietari e la città di Aix-en-Provence che, con il sostegno del ministero della Cultura, sta valutando l'acquisizione di queste opere per il Museo Granet", prosegue la casa d'aste americana. In un'altra asta organizzata dalla casa Christie's, sono state aggiudicate ventisei opere, tra cui due quadri di Claude Monet: "Bord des falaises à Pourville", venduto per 12,7 milioni di euro, e "Trois pots de tulipes", per 3,1 milioni di euro. Un'opera di Pierre-Auguste Renoir, "Jeunes filles au bord de la mer", è stata aggiudicata per 5,8 milioni di euro, mentre "Nature morte au gruyère" di Pablo Picasso ha raggiunto i 3 milioni di euro. Il ricavato complessivo dell'asta di Christie's è pari a 41,6 milioni di euro (commissioni incluse).

items.title: L'Umbria approva la legge sul suicidio medicalmente assistito
items.summary: E' la quinta Regione in Italia ad adottarla. La presidente Proietti non partecipa al voto: 'La dignità umana al centro'
items.content:
Anche l'Umbria - dopo Toscana, Sardegna, Emilia Romagna e Veneto - ha la sua legge sul fine vita. L'Assemblea legislativa ha approvato oggi - con 11 voti favorevoli di consiglieri della maggioranza di centro sinistra, sei contrari e tre astenuti - la proposta di legge di iniziativa popolare, sul suicidio assistito denominata "Liberi subito", nel ricordo di Laura Santi, la giornalista protagonista della battaglia per l'approvazione della norma, malata di sclerosi multipla e morta somministrandosi un farmaco il 21 luglio 2025 nella sua casa di Perugia.

Una figura ed un esempio, i suoi, che hanno pervaso l'intera discussione, anche con ricordi personali da parte di alcuni consiglieri e momenti di commozione. Ad assistere alla riunione, il marito, Stefano Massoli, con un gruppo di attivisti dell'associazione Luca Coscioni e Marco Cappato ("il governo italiano e il Parlamento sono completamente immobili e infilano la testa sotto la sabbia", ha detto). "Questa è la legge di Laura Santi - ha sottolineato il relatore unico Fabrizio Ricci (Avs) - che ci ha lasciato scritto: 'Qualsiasi vita resta degna di essere vissuta anche nelle condizioni più estreme, ma siamo noi a dover scegliere'".

Non ha partecipato al voto la presidente della Regione, Stefania Proietti. "Il tema - ha spiegato - è di una levatura tale che io penso debba essere trattato dal livello politico più alto di cui disponiamo che è il Parlamento, anche per garantire omogenenità". "La mia non partecipazione - ha detto Proietti - va letta come un auspicio: il profumo di rispetto che abbiamo sentito dopo la vicenda di Laura, che io ho seguito per dovere istituzionale come assessorato alla sanità, auspico che resti anche in futuro". "Noi oggi in Umbria - ha sottolineato il vicepresidente della Regione, Tommaso Bori - compiamo una conquista di civiltà, di libertà, di dignità".

Al centro della discussione il tema parallelo delle cure palliative, "una vera priorità" secondo diversi consiglieri. E per Bianca Maria Tagliaferri (Ud-Pp), "il servizio sanitario dovrebbe garantire le cure piuttosto che accompagnare alla morte". Il testo, così come aggiornato dalla Terza commissione, prevede che la Regione disciplini le modalità organizzative di accesso al procedimento di morte volontaria medicalmente assistita mediante autosomministrazione di farmaco letale. Ogni Azienda unità sanitaria locale dovrà istituire una commissione multidisciplinare permanente per la verifica della sussistenza dei requisiti per l'accesso alla morte volontaria medicalmente assistita.

La proposta di legge era sostenuta da 4.801 firme. Nel suo ultimo video Laura Santi aveva affermato: "Dicono che sia un tema divisivo ma in realtà non lo è". Oggi la sua Umbria l'ha ascoltata, in quel "profumo di rispetto della dignità umana, della Costituzione, della vita e della persona, che si è respirato in Aula", come ha sottolineato la presidente Proietti: "Su un un tema di importanza etica assoluta come quello della vita, è stato un segnale per me importante".

items.title: Blocchi dei tir: il governo corre ai ripari, 175 milioni contro il caro carburante
items.summary: Meloni ai camionisti: "Non tolleriamo intimidazioni". Slitta la tassa sui minipacchi
items.content:
Il governo corre ai ripari per disinnescare la bomba sociale dei trasporti e arginare i blocchi stradali che rischiavano di paralizzare il Paese.

Con un decreto-legge varato d'urgenza dal Consiglio dei ministri, l'esecutivo mette sul piatto un pacchetto complessivo da 175 milioni di euro destinato ad autotrasporto, agricoltura e pesca, con i Tir che fanno la parte del leone con 105 milioni. Il decreto inoltre, a sorpresa, fa slittare la tassa sui minipacchi al primo gennaio 2027.

"Il governo ascolta chi manifesta pacificamente", sottolinea la premier Giorgia Meloni. "In alcune zone pochi soggetti continuano a bloccare le strade e non si fermano lì. Minacciano chi vuole lavorare, tagliano le gomme ai camion dei colleghi. Questa non è protesta, è intimidazione e l'intimidazione non la tolleriamo", avverte, promettendo che per garantire la libera circolazione delle merci "useremo tutti gli strumenti che la legge ci offre, comprese le norme del decreto sicurezza che hanno reso reato il blocco stradale".

Il governo non esclude, quindi, la precettazione. La situazione si va sbloccando quasi ovunque, in Sicilia, Puglia, Basilicata, Molise, Calabria con un quasi ritorno alla normalità, mentre in Campania la protesta non rientra del tutto con alcune frange 'deluse' dal decreto del governo: a Napoli un corteo lento di camion ha bloccato l'uscita delle cisterne di carburanti, causando la mancanza di benzina e diesel. Diversi autotrasportatori mantengono ancora presidi fuori dai caselli autostradali della Regione.

Esprime soddisfazione il ministro dei Trasporti, Matteo Salvini. "Abbiamo sbloccato ulteriori risorse e ai tanti piccolini, tanti padroncini con due, tre o quattro mezzi veniamo incontro con il decreto di oggi, con la spalmatura del costo del carburante anche sui committenti, quindi non solo a carico degli autotrasportatori, e con una sospensione fino a tutto marzo 2027 dei leasing che hanno in corso", dice.

Nel dettaglio, per combattere il caro gasolio per i tir vengono destinati ulteriori 45,2 milioni di euro per il credito d'imposta già previsto per il periodo di spesa marzo-agosto 2026. In questo modo l'agevolazione passa da 430 a circa 480 milioni, come annunciato dal viceministro ai Trasporti Edoardo Rixi. Mentre altri 60 milioni sono stanziati per le spese dal primo settembre al 5 ottobre 2026. Ed un'ulteriore boccata d'ossigeno arriva con la proroga dal 1 dicembre 2026 al 1 gennaio 2027 per "l'entrata in vigore del contributo doganale relativo alle spedizioni di modico valore".

"I pagamenti sono iniziati da ieri e quindi entro la prossima settimana le prime 2.000 imprese avranno i crediti di imposta sul cassetto fiscale", dice Rixi in conferenza stampa dopo il cdm. "Si tratta complessivamente, fino alla fine di agosto, di 32.000 imprese e a novembre verrà aperta l'altra finestra per ottobre", aggiunge. Per l'agricoltura vengono allocati 60 milioni di euro e per la pesca 10 milioni, in entrambi i casi come contributi a fondo perduto validi nel 2026.

"Arriveranno in brevissimo tempo attraverso Agea i 60 milioni per il costo del carburante agricolo", assicura il ministro dell'Agricoltura, Francesco Lollobrigida. Servono a "garantire l'acquisto di 121 milioni di litri, con un contributo fino a 45 centesimi", spiega. Le associazioni dell'Autotrasporto iscritte all'albo "apprezzano" l'approvazione immediata delle misure.

"Apprezziamo l'impegno dell'esecutivo per dare risposte concrete a un malcontento che sta diventando sempre più diffuso", afferma il presidente di Conftrasporto e vicepresidente di Confcommercio, Pasquale Russo. Quindi "bene il decreto e le risorse stanziate", sottolinea. Scettica Confimprenditori, secondo cui servivano interventi più incisivi sull'autotrasporto. "Pannicelli caldi, utili a sedare qualche protesta, ma tra qualche mese tutto tornerà com'era prima", avverte il presidente Stefano Ruvolo. Esprime perplessità sul provvedimento anche il Codacons. "Rischia di determinare rincari dei prezzi al dettaglio per l'88% della merce venduta nei negozi", stima l'associazione dei consumatori.

items.title: AI analysis of CT scans finds 42.9% of patients have coronary inflammation
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.biograph.com/newsroom/biograph-completes-first-u.s.-study-with-caristo-diagnostics%E2%80%99-ai-powered-coronary-inflammation-detection-finding-risk-in-over-42-of-asymptomatic-patients Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50198940 Points: 42 # Comments: 24
items.content:
The study evaluated whether AI analysis of coronary inflammation in cardiac CT scans can help identify early cardiovascular risk before symptoms or obstructive plaque appear

The study evaluated whether AI analysis of coronary inflammation in cardiac CT scans can help identify early cardiovascular risk before symptoms or obstructive plaque appear

The study, available to clinically eligible Biograph Black tier members, combined Biograph’s advanced diagnostics – including high-resolution coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) imaging and cardiometabolic profiling – with Caristo’s CaRi-Heart and CaRi-Plaque ® technologies*. This collaborative methodology enabled researchers to assess the prevalence of coronary inflammation using the AI-enabled CaRi-Heart technology to determine cardiovascular risk in individuals who may otherwise appear low risk through traditional screening.

The study found that coronary inflammation is common (42.9%) in asymptomatic, low-risk adults and frequently occurs without any plaque buildup or blockage. Specifically, 42.9% of participants exhibited elevated inflammation with 17.9% of participants exhibiting very high inflammation in at least one major heart artery. The results also suggest a potential limitation in standard assessment: About 47% of participants with no detectable coronary plaque exhibited elevated coronary perivascular inflammation. By evaluating coronary inflammation alongside traditional imaging assessment of plaque burden and stenosis, we get a more complete picture of cardiovascular risk..

Importantly, routine bloodwork and clinical tools – including cholesterol markers (ApoB, non-HDL-C), blood sugar (HbA1c), systemic inflammation (hs-CRP), and a widely used cardiovascular risk calculator (AHA PREVENT-ASCVD) – showed no correlation with the presence of coronary inflammation and failed to identify which patients had inflamed arteries. These results reinforce Biograph’s core philosophy: standalone bloodwork and isolated metrics do not tell the full story. By directly analyzing the biology of the tissue surrounding the coronary arteries, this non-invasive AI technology uncovers potential cardiovascular risk years before the onset of irreversible heart disease.

For Biograph, the completion of this study reflects its broader mission to advance proactive, personalized healthcare through comprehensive diagnostics, clinical interpretation, and earlier insight into long-term health risks. To review the clinical study manuscript, readers can access the published preprint here.

*CaRi-Heart® has received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) De Novo marketing authorization and is the first and only solution to quantify coronary inflammation from routine coronary CT angiography (CCTA). CaRi-Plaque® has received U.S. FDA clearance for AI-assisted coronary plaque and stenosis analysis, complementing CaRi-Heart by evaluating quantitative plaque.

Because how well you live is as important as how long you live. With an emphasis on human centered design, we've created an unparalleled clinical facility to defy industry norms. items.title: Show HN: agent-usage-guard – a Claude Code mod to protect your usage window
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/rbartoli/agent-usage-guard Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50198936 Points: 13 # Comments: 6
items.content:
Stops Claude Code from spending your five-hour usage window in ten minutes.

agent-usage-guard is a Claude Code mod : it runs inside Claude Code and holds runaway spend before it happens. It reads your plan's live usage, and it holds subagent fan-out, heavy-context churn and retry loops.

Recorded from Claude Code's interactive UI with the guard loaded. A scripted local API stands in for Claude, so the sessions and token counts are staged and no usage is spent. Every question on screen is the guard's own. Rebuild it from the Northstar fixture .

It acts before the spend, not after it: before an agent starts, a prompt is sent, or a tool call runs. Agent limits hold across every Claude Code session on your machine, and fan-out and heavy context are capped at any usage level, not only near the limit. When you are at the keyboard it asks you, in Claude Code's own question dialog. When nobody can answer, it refuses and tells Claude why, so the model can wait, batch the work, or stop. /agent-guard report shows what it did.

Then run /agent-guard to see what it sees. Mods are on by default; the overview lists the settings that turn them off.

One afternoon I gave Claude Code a research prompt at max effort. It spawned 394 subagent calls, 341 of them running at once, and pushed 84M context tokens through the API in ten minutes. Session over: "Claude usage limit reached." Locked out until the window reset.

That wasn't a one-off. Sixty days of my own logs held 12 lockouts and 166 ten-minute windows with agent bursts. The failure mode multiplies: a large context × rapid tool loops × parallel agents × blind retries . Each protection below removes one factor.

And it's not just me: 339 subagents from a single prompt , half a weekly Max plan consumed by recursive spawning , and multi-agent runs using ~15× the tokens of a chat session .

Agents covers subagents, agent-team teammates, workflow agents, and finished subagents resumed with SendMessage . Each tool call is judged on the context of the loop that makes it, so a small subagent never inherits the main conversation's size.

When it asks. The question appears in Claude Code's own dialog, the one Claude uses to ask you something, and the call waits for your answer. Agents started in parallel while it is open are held back, and Claude starts them again once you answer. If you allow it, that condition stays allowed for a while: a plan window until it resets, a heavy context until it shrinks (for tool calls, an hour at most), the agent counts for 10 minutes. If you decline or dismiss the question, Claude is told not to start agents for the next 10 minutes ( AGENT_GUARD_WINDOW_SECONDS ), and is not asked again in that time. Typed words reach Claude, so you can answer "use haiku agents instead".

When nobody can answer. In claude -p , the Agent SDK and dontAsk mode, an agent or tool gate refuses instead of asking. A heavy prompt is held with the reason, and so is a dormant heavy resume once the machine-wide cap of one per 10 minutes is reached. Claude reads each refusal as the tool's result. Repeat refusals of the same condition are worded differently each time and escalate: the second says nothing has changed and to try something else, the third says to end the turn. If a Stop hook such as /goal keeps reopening the turn, the refusal says the user has to decide.

What it leaves alone. It never holds a background task's notification or another session's message, because that would lose the result. It no longer blocks prompts after a usage limit: since v2.1.234, Claude Code waits at a limit and continues at reset on its own ( autoContinueAtUsageLimit ). The guard's job is to keep you from reaching the limit, and its journal counts the lockouts it did not prevent.

/agent-guard runs at once, even mid-turn, and never starts a model turn, so Claude never sees an override and cannot take one as permission. Sending [allow-usage-guard] or [allow-agent-burst] alone as a prompt, the markers of earlier versions, does the same as /agent-guard allow or allow agents .

Mods run in claude in a terminal, in the Desktop app's Code tab, in claude -p and the Agent SDK. They don't run in a Desktop-app WSL session ( where mods run ).

Native limits still matter. Claude Code caps a session at 20 concurrent subagents ( CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS ) and three layers of nesting ( CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH ). It has no limit on the total number of agents a session starts. The guard's defaults are stricter and span sessions; the native caps remain the outer wall for the paths the guard only counts.

The report counts usage-limit lockouts (each locked window once), plan-window threshold crossings, and every question and refusal by rule, with what you answered. It reads every session's journal on this machine and never leaves it. Set AGENT_GUARD_JOURNAL=0 to stop recording.

A mod runs inside Claude Code with your permissions; read what a mod can reach before you install one. This one is about 2,400 lines of TypeScript with no dependencies, and claude plugin validate . lists every API it calls and every environment variable it reads:

Set these as environment variables, or under env in ~/.claude/settings.json . Times are in seconds; a value that isn't a number in range keeps its default, and /agent-guard says so.

The dormant default assumes the one-hour prompt cache that subscriptions get within plan usage. With an API key or extra usage, the cache lasts five minutes, so set AGENT_GUARD_DORMANT_SECONDS=300 .

The rules live in a harness-agnostic core ( core/ ) that performs no I/O. The Claude Code mod is its first adapter. docs/architecture.md describes the contract an adapter keeps and what another agent harness must offer to carry each rule.

claude plugin test runs the suite inside Claude Code's own test kit: unit tests of the core, and tests that fire real Claude Code events through the hooks module with no session, model or network. TESTING.md covers the layers and what each test proves.

items.title: La famiglia Vacchi compra l'Hotel de La Poste di Cortina d'Ampezzo
items.summary: L'iconico albergo passa sotto il controllo degli industriali bolognesi del packaging
items.content:
Cortina Holding Srl, veicolo partecipato dalla holding Alva Spa facente capo alla famiglia del presidente e ad di Ima Alberto Vacchi, ha acquistato dalle famiglie Manaigo ed Esposito l'Hotel de la Poste di Cortina d'Ampezzo.

Fondato nel 1804 e situato in piazza Roma, l'albergo è una delle strutture alberghiere storiche della Regina delle Dolomiti. Composto da 73 stanze, l'hotel verrà riqualificato per diventare un 5 stelle lusso. Il progetto prevede di realizzare una struttura di 55 tra camere e suite di ampia metratura e un'offerta di servizi coerente con il posizionamento luxury. Previsti inoltre il restauro dello storico Bar del Posta, due ristoranti, una spa e spazi per eventi privati.

Il cda della società che gestirà l'albergo sarà gestito da Gregorio Minelli Vacchi, figlio di Alberto Vacchi. L'hotel resterà aperto fino all'inizio dei lavori di ristrutturazione e verrà garantita la continuità dell'attività sia nella gestione che nello staff. "La mia famiglia resta profondamente impegnata nel mondo industriale, ma pensiamo che riqualificare l'Hotel de la Poste sia un'impresa piena di sfide e di opportunità, non solo economiche. Mio figlio Gregorio sarà impegnato in questa iniziativa che richiede molte energie ed idee innovative che possono venire solo dai giovani", ha commentato Alberto Vacchi, che guida la storica azienda di Ozzano dell'Emilia (Bologna) del packaging.

items.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50198675 Points: 141 # Comments: 71
items.content:
New in OpenShell 0.1.x: a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives, an expanded extension surface, and new APIs. Read the 0.1.0 upgrade guide .

OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials. OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network. You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it.

OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied.

See Architecture for how the gateway, supervisor, and sandbox fit together.

You need Linux, macOS on Apple Silicon, or Windows with WSL 2 (experimental), plus Docker, Podman, or host virtualization. See the Support Matrix for details.

The installer sets up the CLI and a local gateway. The default sandbox image is minimal Ubuntu with no agent installed. To run a real agent, follow Run Your First Agent : it runs OpenCode against a free OpenRouter model and shows how to approve new access as the agent needs it.

The skills teach your agent to drive the OpenShell CLI, write sandbox policies, and debug gateways and inference routing. They live in skills/ and work without an OpenShell source checkout.

SDKs connect applications to an OpenShell gateway. They do not install the CLI. Use the same OpenShell release for the SDK and the gateway when possible.

items.title: M5s a Strasburgo vota come Vannacci: no a missione contro russi nel Mar Nero. Riformisti pd critici
items.summary: Sensi: “Mi vergogno per loro”. Quartapelle: “Sarebbe bello e doveroso che spiegassero perché”
items.content:
La delegazione del Movimento 5 stelle al Parlamento europeo ha votato contro la risoluzione su "L'intensificazione degli attacchi russi nell'area del Mar Nero" in cui si chiede di valutare il dispiegamento di un'operazione navale Ue nel Mar Nero . Tra le ragioni vi sarebbe proprio questa richiesta e il fatto che il testo sia tutto incentrato sull'escalation. Oltre al M5s, hanno votato contro solo una parte minoritaria del Patrioti e il gruppo di estrema destra 'Europa delle nazioni sovrane'. È quanto risulta dall'analisi del voto.

La risoluzione è stata approvata a larga maggioranza (432 voti a favore) con il sostegno di quasi tutte le forze (Ppe, S&d, Renew, Ecr, Verdi). I Patrioti si sono astenuti per la gran parte, con la delegazione austriaca che ha votato contro. La maggior parte del gruppo The Left, di cui fa parte il M5s, si è astenuta, mentre alcuni hanno votato a favore.

Un voto che attira le critiche dei riformisti del Pd. "Non capisco perché quella congiunzione tra destra e M5s, Giorgio, mi vergogno per loro, mentre Kyiv viene bombardata", scrive sui social il senatore dem Filippo Sensi , commentando un post in cui l'eurodeputato Giorgio Gori scrive che "a Strasburgo, risoluzione contro l'escalation di attacchi russi nell'Ue, e in particolare nel Mar Nero. Approvata a larghissima maggioranza. Contraria l'estrema destra. E i colleghi del M5s".

Anche Lia Quartapelle interviene sui social: "Sarebbe bello e doveroso che il M5s spiegasse perché, insieme all'estrema destra, ha votato contro una risoluzione che denuncia gli attacchi russi nell'Ue e sul Mar Nero. Dubito che accada: sarebbe come ammettere che non vogliono proteggere l'Europa e preferiscono la Russia".

items.content: Un decoratore in pensione è diventato milionario dopo aver venduto all'asta una collezione di carte Pokémon. Lo riporta la Bbc. La sua collezione, rimasta in soffitta per 15 anni, è stata battuta all'asta da Ewbank's per 1,56 milioni di sterline. "Quando abbiamo visto cosa possedesse - tutto in condizioni perfette, come nuovo - non riuscivamo a crederci", ha dichiarato James Spooner, responsabile del dipartimento carte collezionabili. La casa d'aste del Surrey ha aggiunto che questa vendita è stata la più fruttuosa nei suoi oltre 30 anni, ipotizzando che possa trattarsi addirittura di un record europeo. Il pezzo forte è stato il "Legendary Collection Complete Master Set", che includeva una carta di Charizard in condizioni quasi perfette. La stima iniziale era compresa tra 15.000 e 20.000 sterline, ma il ricavato ha raggiunto le 100.000 sterline. Secondo la casa d'aste Ewbank's, questa cifra record per la collezione Pokémon ha superato il precedente primato, stabilito appena il 9 ottobre a Londra, quando un'asta presso Stanley Gibbons aveva totalizzato 872.000 sterline.

items.content:
"La cosa che mi meraviglia è la meraviglia verso questo gesto" che "è una cosa normale, ho fatto il magistrato tutta la vita forse questo fa la differenza....".Così la deputata della Lega Simonetta Matone conferma al telefono quanto anticipato da alcuni quotidiani sul suo ritrovamento di un prezioso anello nei bagni della Camera che ha subito riconsegnato ai commessi perché se ne cercasse il proprietario.

items.content:
Clavicular, a social media influencer who promotes the "looksmaxxing" trend of young men maximising their attractiveness, has pleaded not guilty to criminal charges including rape.

The 20-year-old, whose real name is Braden Peters, was charged in September with felony rape, drugging an individual for sexual intercourse and procuring alcohol for someone under the age of 21.

The charges stem from an incident in 2025 when he is accused of assaulting a 17-year-old girl at his family's Massachusetts home.

Peters has denied the allegations and said the encounter was consensual. On Thursday, he was granted $10,000 bail, ordered not to contact or post about his accuser, and to surrender his passport.

A woman told police that on 23 May 2025, Peters ordered her an Uber to his family's house in Chatham where they were drinking alcohol while filming a livestream before he allegedly raped her, according to the BBC's US partner, CBS News.

The police officer who took the report said he believed she was unable to consent due to her age and the level of intoxication she exhibited in the livestream, CBS reported.

Clavicular has more than a million followers on TikTok and Instagram and has garnered media attention for extreme measures he has taken for "looksmaxxing".

He has admitted to using a hammer on his face and jawline and taking a number of steroids, injections, and other drugs to achieve bodily perfection. He also gives advice on appearing masculine and performs stunts to shock followers.

In Florida earlier this year, he was charged after filming himself shooting at what appeared to be a dead alligator. He pleaded no contest to unlawfully discharging a firearm in public.

In March, he was arrested on suspicion of battery after authorities suspected him of instigating a fight between two women. Authorities said in July that they did not intend to file charges.

After Thursday's hearing, Peters posted a photo of himself in the black suit and black tie he wore to court, while holding his dog which he also brought to court.

His next hearing will be on 24 November, when the judge will decide if there is enough evidence for the case to move forward.

items.title: 'Demeaning' and 'absurd': The backlash against a hugging grandparents consent ad
items.summary: Jim O'Callaghan described the video as "inappropriate and demeaning to grandparents".
items.content:
It's the consent campaign that's sparked heated debate across Ireland and beyond - so why has a social media ad about getting a hug from your grandparents been pulled?

The ad, described by an Irish government minister as "demeaning to grandparents", sees a house's front door opening to reveal an elderly couple.

They hug their grandson and lean into embrace their granddaughter, who looks uncomfortable before it quickly cuts to a graphic and voiceover.

"Not everyone wants a hug. Even from the people who love them. Awkward? Maybe. Important? Absolutely."

The tone is light-hearted, and the aim is to promote the importance of consent for children - but it has apparently landed with a thud in Ireland and with many online.

The ad, one of three, is part of a campaign called We-Consent, run by the Dublin Rape Crisis Centre (DRCC).

The backlash has opened up a debate about changing norms, the role of family and how best to teach consent to children.

While some have described it as a waste of money, others have defended it as showing how children have differences when it comes to boundaries and that it is "not campaigning against grandparents".

Irish Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan has been an instrumental critic - his department is one of the sources of funding for the campaign and its removal came after his officials intervened.

He said the video "does not represent the views of the government".

"It was both inappropriate and demeaning to grandparents and has been removed by DRCC following my officials engagement with them.

"While it is vital to ensure that people understand the concept of consent when it comes to sexual relationships, this video did not advance that aim and in many ways was counterproductive."

In a statement to Irish broadcaster RTÉ, the DRCC said the videos were "premised on the idea that boundaries should be respected from an early age and to respect others' boundaries too".

"We are going to remove the videos from our social media channels while we reflect on whether they are having the positive effect we want them to have," it added.

Fine Gael Senator Gareth Scahill, who is among the critics, said the video was a waste of resources.

"What's concerning here is public money has been used to fund an ad which at best has been ill-thought out, and at worst is offensive and potentially damaging to our older population," he said, adding that this "publicly-funded social media video is a million miles off the mark".

"What's next? Will we need to sign consent forms at arrival halls in Dublin, Shannon, Knock and Cork airports this Christmas before we can greet family members?"

A spokesperson for the Department of Justice said the videos were "produced by DRCC at low cost using volunteers and are not part of a government advertising campaign".

Meanwhile, Dr Eoin O'Malley, an associate professor at Dublin City University, said he believes the advert is the latest example of the state overreaching.

"You are seeing people pushing ideas that are beyond mainstream," he said.

O'Malley said that the importance of consent is reasonable to most people, but that the video is too extreme.

"The idea that there needs to be an ad telling grandparents that they shouldn't hug their grandkids, that they should look for permission in advance of that, seems absurd to most normal people.

"The Irish constitution is very clear that the family is the primary unit for teaching children and for raising children, and so to some extent this is kind of going beyond that."

Academic Dr Órfhlaith Campbell said it is not an attack on grandparents but instead aimed to highlight the importance of consent.

"The ad is highlighting differences in children's needs and the imp (sic) of consent. It is not campaigning against grandparents. Dear god in heaven!!!" she wrote on X , external .

An account named Danny Boy said it wasn't "discouraging grandparents from hugging children" but was "encouraging children to speak up" if they feel uncomfortable.

University of Galway academic Dr Eoin Daly said that while the video was "patronising", the message was correct.

Fine Gael councillor Lorraine Hall also defended the advert, and said the message of the video was intended to be "figurative" rather than "literal".

items.title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit
items.summary: Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave in 2021.
items.content:
A US judge has ordered President Donald Trump to answer questions under oath in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by 11 December.

Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021.

Charles Tobin, a lawyer representing the BBC, said in court that "we still haven't been able to depose the plaintiff" with two months left in the discovery period, during which both sides are legally required to exchange information with each other on their case.

Trump cancelled a previous deposition on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance" while he was campaigning in Georgia.

In US law, a deposition is an out-of-court statement made under oath in response to questions, which is recorded for use in later proceedings.

The judge in the case, US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett, said that Trump must sit for the deposition by 11 December, unless the discovery period is extended.

Last week, attorneys asked that Lett compel Trump to face deposition after the last scheduled meeting did not take place.

On that day, Trump attended a midterms campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia and a fundraiser at his property in Mar-a-Lago in Florida.

In a separate filing on Wednesday, Trump's lawyers said that the president could appear for the interview between 11 and 22 January next year, and claimed that the BBC was "wrong to claim that President Trump is avoiding his deposition in this action."

Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously, and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021.

The BBC apologised for the error and said that the broadcast gave "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action".

The broadcaster has since asked that the court dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the programme does not meet the legal criteria for defamation and was not available in the US.

In July, Trump's lawyers conceded that they had no evidence that the documentary was available in the US on the BBC's BritBox subscription service - as they originally claimed - or on the BBC's website, BBC select or through US broadcasters.

Trump ultimately agreed to drop the lawsuit against BBC Studios, its commercial arm, after the BBC argued that it had "no role in creating or producing the documentary".

Typically, depositions take place in a lawyer's office - rather than a courtroom - without a judge physically present.

Depositions, however, carry legal weight and take place under oath. They are recorded verbatim by a court reporter, and the transcripts can later be used as evidence during trials.

In defamation cases, lawyers for both sides are normally present for depositions.

items.title: Race to update services' computer systems after cyber-security flaw found
items.summary: Websites were taken offline after the developers of programming language PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" had been discovered.
items.content:
Organisations and businesses are still scrambling to update their systems after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a widely-used programming language, PHP.

Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday after the developers of PHP said "critical vulnerabilities" were found in the back-end language, used in web development for decades.

Researchers warned the "severe" flaws could expose millions of sites using it to potential hacks if left unpatched - and the UK government was among those to take some sites offline as a precaution.

There have been no successful attacks reported so far, but experts say any impact may take time - even months - to become fully apparent.

Downing Street said on Thursday "some" limited government services "may be offline" while security work was being carried out.

"The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra told the House of Lords.

She attributed this to having "largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied".

The government did not specify which services were taken offline - but it said no large UK public-facing critical services had been affected.

A spokesperson said work had already taken place across government to "identify and fix potential exposures to our systems and our experts are continuing to work closely with both OpenAI and international partners on this issue".

"But this does not mean they were hacked, and work continues to resolve any issues," they added.

Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), called the event "unprecedented".

"It will be universally felt, I suspect," he told BBC Radio 4's World At One.

But he said there were "no indications" of any successful breaches by hackers.

He said the NCSC was "starting to see positive confirmation" that advice sent to those affected , external had been received and was being acted on.

Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble?

Cyber-security lecturer Rory Hopcraft told the BBC the government needed to make sure that its own infrastructure was up-to-date.

"The government are the ones who set the rules for other organisations... they just need to effectively be practising what they're preaching at this point."

Dean Presley, who has a garage in Chepstow, South Wales, told BBC Your Voice he had been unable to properly process MOTs online.

He said his computer system had been down since Wednesday morning, and while he has experienced outages before, they have not lasted this long.

"MOTs can be conducted and they're legal but none of the paperwork and certificates can be printed and they're not on the system," Dean said.

He said this has forced him to write everything on paper documents, leading to delays for customers.

It's a programming language which runs on a web server, behind the scenes of a website, and effectively lets you see the sites you visit.

When you go to a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.

It was developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, but still powers lots of platforms today.

PHP has been used across a wide range of platforms including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites - as well as to write tools to build web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.

According to cyber-security firm Wiz , external , which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.

And it said the flaws - now coined "php2shell" - were inherent in the language itself, affecting many past versions of it.

The PHP Foundation, the non-profit which maintains the programming language, warned this meant that, under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker would be able to remotely execute code on servers running PHP.

Some large organisations said they had seen a high volume of attempts to breach their systems.

Matthew Prince, the boss of internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, wrote on X , external on Thursday that the company saw "thousands" of attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerabilities across its network in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.

"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," he added.

Amazon also says it saw hackers attempt to exploit the flaws, but its websites were operating as normal.

While the impact of the PHP flaw remains to be seen, disruption continued for businesses and organisations after many sites were taken down on Wednesday.

The website of a Dutch agency specialising in cyber-security, Finland's government and parts of Wikipedia, taken temporarily offline, had returned to business as usual by Thursday.

But a number of sites appeared to have been taken offline on Thursday, as operators rushed to check if PHP might be running within their systems or if any patches were required.

In France, telecommunications company Orange also said , external it had suspended access to certain services globally while it deployed security fixes.

According to some cyber-security researchers using scans to check servers at risk of the PHP vulnerability, the rate of organisations implementing patches - but not as quickly as might be hoped globally.

"The window to respond has shrunk dramatically," said Matt Hull, VP of cyber intelligence and response at global cyber security company NCC Group.

"A few years ago, attackers might have taken weeks to exploit a vulnerability. Now, it can be days or hours."

Hull also highlighted the extent of the task facing developers and engineers working to deal with the issue.

"Several days into this incident, security professionals might already be dealing with significant burnout," he said, urging a need to "make time to rest, share the workload and look after each other".

items.title: Germany target of 'intensive' espionage, Merz says after suspected Russian spy arrest
items.summary: A Ukrainian man was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia - one of several such cases in Germany this year.
items.content:
Germany is the target of "intensive" espionage activity, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said after a Ukrainian national was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia.

Officials said the suspect, named as Vadym Y., had allegedly collected military-related intelligence from Germany.

Merz called the uncovering of the case a "success", but warned "let us not delude ourselves - the activities of Russian intelligence services in Germany remain at a consistently high level".

Several people alleged to be acting on behalf of Russia and other foreign powers have been arrested in Germany this year. Germany has been one of the leading European suppliers of weapons to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

The German Federal Prosecutor General's Office said on Thursday that Vadym Y., as he was identified under German privacy law, had been in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025.

It also said the Ukrainian man had collected information including "on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives".

He is due to appear before an investigating judge on Friday.

In January, a woman was arrested in Berlin suspected of gathering information for an intelligence officer at the Russian embassy.

Other arrests this year included a Romanian woman and a Ukrainian man accused of spying on an individual supplying drones from Germany to Ukraine, according to the prosecutor's office.

UK and Germany will face threats together, says Burnham in Berlin

Trial of German steakhouse heiress that sparked a huge spy scandal

Sabotage suspect held in Germany after spate of attacks on power grid

And, the former German spy chief August Hanning was arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power earlier this month. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.

Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.

Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D and accused him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents in exchange for money.

Speaking at the sidelines of a conference in Montenegro on Thursday, Merz said: "We will likely see more such cases in the coming months and years."

Merz reaffirmed a series of defence and security partnerships with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham earlier this month, including tackling hybrid attacks and hostile activity.

The talks between the two leaders came after Germany accused Russia of launching a drone fitted with explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport in September.

Russian President Vladimir Putin accused Germany of planting evidence to blame Russia.

items.title: Lula says rival should be disqualified over alleged Meta interference ahead of Brazil vote
items.summary: The Brazilian president accuses the tech firm of favouring Flávio Bolsonaro, which it denies.
items.content:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's campaign has requested the disqualification of right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in the lead up to the final round of the presidential election on Sunday over alleged interference by social media company Meta.

In a petition filed to the country's top electoral court on Wednesday, the leftist incumbent president accused Meta, the tech giant behind Whatsapp, Instagram and Facebook, of limiting its content to boost Bolsonaro's campaign.

In response, Bolsonaro filed a petition seeking to disqualify Lula over what he said was the mass dissemination of government posts on WhatsApp.

The company has denied the campaigns have been treated unequally.

It comes after UN experts said on Wednesday that they were concerned about reports of discrepancies in the ability of each campaign to reach voters on Meta's platforms.

A report led by the UN's special rapporteur on freedom of expression said Meta must ensure a level playing field online during the election.

It cited incidents including "temporary interruptions of one candidate's campaign account; differences in audience engagement, user feeds, view counts and reach; restrictions on that campaign's Instagram posts".

"Information, including from Meta employees, suggests that accounts linked to one side of the presidential race were disproportionately curtailed," it read.

Meta has denied taking action to favour one side of the election and has said it would comply with an order from a Brazilian court to treat Bolsonaro and Lula equally.

Lula's campaign had previously filed a complaint alleging that accounts and content related to Bolsonaro were boosted.

Users also reported that Meta's artificial intelligence tools were not generating images related to Lula.

Brazilians will head to the polls on Sunday as Lula seeks a fourth term in office.

Bolsonaro beat Lula in the first round of voting on 4 October by a narrow margin, but fell short of the 50% of valid votes needed to win outright.

On Wednesday, Lula's campaign filed a petition to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) for Bolsonaro and Alfredo Gaspar, his candidate for vice-president, to be investigated over "abuse of economic power and improper use of social network".

The petition also seeks to make Bolsonaro ineligible to stand for election for eight years following the 2026 election.

Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, accused his rival of "abuse of political and economic power".

He claims the government has used personal data taken from official databases to send mass messages on Whatsapp to promote social programmes.

Opinion polls suggest Sunday's run-off will be extremely close, with little separating the two as Brazil's 159 million registered voters prepare to go to the ballot boxes.

Brazil's Congress approves shorter working week in win for Lula

items.title: Aggredisce i fan fuori da una discoteca, denunciato Fedez
items.summary: Esposto in procura di quattro giovani padovani, gli avevano chiesto un selfie. 'Un pugno dal rapper e calci dalle guardie del corpo'
items.content:
Prima le minacce, "se rimani qui le prendi", poi le botte. Un pugno in pieno volto, seguito dai calci delle guardie del corpo. È finita al pronto soccorso la serata in un locale della movida milanese di due fratelli padovani e dei loro amici, 'colpevoli' di avere chiesto un selfie a Federico Leonardo Lucia, in arte Fedez.

Il rapper, già coinvolto in passato in episodi del genere, è stato denunciato per lesioni personali dai ragazzi, che nei suoi confronti hanno presentato una querela con allegati i video dell'aggressione. La Procura di Milano ha aperto un fascicolo e presto potrebbero esserci i primi indagati. I legali del cantante, Gabriele Minniti e Andrea Petrolucci, sostengono che abbia "reagito a una aggressione subita da alcuni giovani in evidente stato di alterazione". E annunciano querele nei confronti di chi "riporti ricostruzioni difformi dai fatti realmente accaduti".

Eppure nelle dodici pagine presentate alla Procura di Milano dagli avvocati Alberto Berardi, Giuseppe Lombardino e Paolo Tabasso, tutti del foro di Padova, la ricostruzione di quanto accaduto sembra essere molto circostanziata. I fatti risalgono alla sera del 16 ottobre, un venerdì. Per festeggiare un amico in partenza per l'Australia, i due fratelli decidono di passare qualche ora in una discoteca di corso Garibaldi.

Tra brindisi e balli, è quasi mattina quando si appostano fuori per cercare di fermare Artie 5ive, un altro rapper anche lui presente nel locale. È in quel momento che si imbattono in Fedez e decidono di chiedergli un selfie. "Dai che altrimenti va a finire male", replica a muso duro il cantante, che il giorno prima aveva festeggiato il 37esimo compleanno. Nel video ripreso col cellulare si sente il più giovane dei fratelli rispondere all'autore di 'Vorrei ma non posto' "no no, hai ragione" prima di allontanarsi con gli altri ragazzi. Poco dopo, però, il rapper lo avrebbe colpito con un pugno in volto, dando poi ordine di inseguirli alle sue guardie del corpo.

Uno avrebbe preso a calci il 19enne fino a farlo svenire. Trasportato al pronto soccorso del Policlinico è stato dimesso con quattro giorni di prognosi. Uno in meno, invece, per il fratello 21enne e un paio per gli altri due amici. Già un paio di anni fa, ricordano nella querela gli avvocati, il rapper avrebbe aggredito un suo fan. Ed è di pochi giorni prima dell'aggressione denunciata che il cameriere di un locale milanese ha accusato il cantante di averlo picchiato per avergli scattato una foto con il cellulare.

items.title: Scoperto l'enzima Pac-Man: mangia la plastica in 250 giorni
items.summary: Un enzima batterico chiamato Pac-Man aiuta a degradare le bioplastiche nel terreno in meno di un anno.
items.content:
Abbiamo scoperto a spese del pianeta che la plastica è uno dei materiali più difficili da eliminare dall'ambiente, soprattutto perché molti dei polimeri utilizzati oggi resistono per decenni, frammentandosi progressivamente in microplastiche. E queste sono poi un rischio crescente per la nostra salute, visto che siamo circondati da oggetti fatti di questo materiale.

Esistono delle alternative biodegradabili che promettono di ridurre questo problema, ma la loro effettiva decomposizione dipende dalle condizioni ambientali e dall'attività dei microrganismi presenti. La buona notizia è che una ricerca condotta dall'Università di Costanza, in Germania, ha individuato un particolare enzima batterico capace di attaccare direttamente alcune bioplastiche, consentendo ai microrganismi di utilizzarle come fonte di nutrimento. Gli scienziati lo hanno soprannominato Pac-Man, richiamando curiosamente una similitudine tra il gioco e il modo in cui contribuisce a consumare il materiale.

Per capire quanto fosse efficace questo processo, i ricercatori hanno mescolato bioplastiche appartenenti alla famiglia dei poliesteri alifatici a catena lunga (LCAP) con campioni di terreno forestale. Monitorando per oltre un anno la produzione di anidride carbonica, utilizzata come indicatore dell'attività metabolica dei microrganismi, hanno osservato una degradazione pressoché completa dei materiali analizzati nell'arco di 250-330 giorni.

Parliamo della possibilità di far lavorare un'intelligenza artificiale direttamente sul proprio computer, lasciando documenti, email e informazioni personali al sicuro sul dispositivo. items.title: Peugeot 204 Coupé e Cabriolet, le regine degli anni '60 tornano a Bologna
items.summary: Il Club Storico Peugeot Italia ha festeggiato i 60 anni della Peugeot 204 Coupé e Cabriolet con una presenza speciale
items.content:
All'evento Auto e Moto d'Epoca, in programma a BolognaFiere dal 22 al 25 ottobre 2026, il Club Storico Peugeot ricorderà due regine degli anni '60. I fari saranno puntati sulla 204 Coupé e Cabriolet, interpretazioni del fascino senza tempo transalpino. La Peugeot 204 Cabriolet, selezionata per omaggiare il sessantesimo anniversario del modello, ha lasciato un impronta indelebile negli appassionati del marchio del Leone.Prodotta tra il 1965 ed il 1976, la 204 divenne un'auto generazionale, facendo capolino nel segmento delle vetture di categoria medio-bassa, dopo l'uscita di scena della 202 alla fine degli anni '40. La prima grande Peugeot di serie ad adottare la trazione anteriore, con motore montato trasversalmente, si distingueva per soluzioni tecniche all'avanguardia, come le sospensioni indipendenti su entrambi gli assi e i freni anteriori a disco. Il cuore pulsante era un quattro cilindri da 1.130 cm³, con monoblocco e testata in lega leggera, che garantiva performance, leggerezza ed efficienza.

Un'icona senza tempo

La presentazione ufficiale della 204 avvenne il 23 aprile del 1965 al Palasport di Parigi. La tre volumi di taglia ridotta, a differenza delle sorelle in listino, aveva un linguaggio stilistico identitario, molto distante dai canoni americani così in voga ai tempi. Le linee sinuose, compatte ed eleganti inaugurarono un nuovo concetto di raffinatezza europea che poi segnò tutte le Peugeot successive.Nel 1966 il listino della Casa francese venne impreziosito dalle versioni Coupé e Cabriolet, che reinterpretavano in chiave più personale e dinamica le linee della berlina. Con una lunghezza di circa 3,73 metri, le due varianti vantavano un passo accorciato e una carrozzeria identitaria, sviluppata dal Centro Stile Peugeot diretto da Paul Bouvot, anche con un pizzico di italianità targato Pininfarina.

La Cabrio del popolo

La biposto senza tetto spiccava per una silhouette bassa e slanciata con una capote ripiegabile. La meccanica telaistica delle 204 coupé e cabriolet non presentava grosse differenze rispetto alla berlina. I prezzi erano accessibili e il successo fu una naturale conseguenza. Chi cercava versatilità e sportività sceglieva la Coupé con una configurazione a tre porte e il portellone posteriore. Sotto al cofano c'era un brillante motore anteriore trasversale, associato a un cambio manuale a quattro rapporti.Il quattro cilindri da 1.130 cm³, in una fase iniziale, arrivava a 53 CV, una potenza in linea con le caratteristiche di una linea leggera e progettata per offrire performance divertenti e una buona abitabilità. Oggi sarebbero considerate proposte scomode e minuscole, ma lo stile compatto non è passato di moda e farà scendere qualche lacrimuccia agli appassionati che parteciperanno al Club Storico Peugeot Italia nella prossima edizione di Auto e Moto d'Epoca.[drivek_widget brand_id="peugeot" model_id="2008"]

items.title: Computer quantistici, raggiunta una precisione del 99,9995%
items.summary: Helios raggiunge una fedeltà del 99,9995% grazie a un nuovo sistema di correzione degli errori.
items.content:
C'è un ostacolo, considerato piuttosto ostico, che separa i computer quantistici dalle applicazioni pratiche. Si tratta della loro affidabilità, perché se da un lato queste macchine promettono di affrontare calcoli estremamente complessi, dall'altro i qubit, ovvero le unità fondamentali dell'informazione quantistica, sono così delicati che anche piccole interferenze possono compromettere i risultati.

Si sta cercando di ridurre gli errori, e questa è considerata una delle sfide decisive per rendere questa tecnologia realmente utilizzabile. Un risultato particolarmente interessante arriva da Quantinuum, che con il suo computer quantistico Helios ha raggiunto una fedeltà logica del 99,9995%, equivalente ad appena cinque errori ogni milione di cicli di correzione.

Si tratta di un miglioramento di dieci volte rispetto al precedente record ottenuto dalla stessa azienda nel settembre 2026. Secondo Quantinuum, il tasso di errore è inoltre cento volte inferiore al miglior risultato precedentemente pubblicato su un sistema superconduttore di Google Quantum AI, sebbene il confronto riguardi specifiche misure di affidabilità.

items.title: Mini brain organoids 'reading' Braille key step towards biohybrid computing
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.frontiersin.org/news/2026/10/16/mini-brain-organoids-reading-braille-biohybrid-computing-frontiers-artificial-intelligence Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50197450 Points: 21 # Comments: 12
items.content:
A group of scientists have shown that brain organoids can pass on signals that correspond to Braille letters, an essential step towards developing the energy-efficient biohybrid computers of the future. The brain organoids, remotely connected to a sensor that recorded tactile signals from different Braille letters, produced signals that were different for each letter, allowing a decoder to distinguish between the different letters the organoids had been given. Although individual brain organoids provided accurately decodable signals 61% of the time, a team of three performed significantly better, producing an accurate signal 83% of the time. The team of three was also better at distinguishing the signals from artificial noise than the decoder working directly on the obscured signals, without the organoids’ involvement.

Could computers include tiny brain organoids one day? The human brain is an incredibly energy-efficient computer, and silicon processors that try to imitate it achieve huge energy savings over traditional processors. Now scientists are experimenting with using organoids modelled on the human forebrain to develop energy-efficient biohybrid computing. A crucial first step towards this is learning whether the organoids can receive and relay signals reliably, which a Bristol-based team of researchers investigated using Braille letters. They found that teams of three brain organoids produced signals which accurately corresponded to different letters 83% of the time.

“We can take information from a real tactile sensor, turn it into a form that a living neural network can receive, and then recover meaningful information from the organoid response,” said Tianyi Liu, PhD candidate at Bristol University and first author of the article in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence . “That gives us a practical way to connect artificial sensors with biological neural systems, which are a very interesting possible route towards more energy-efficient computing.”

The biohybrid systems tested by Liu and her team use brain organoids placed on multielectrode arrays and contained in a system that keeps the organoids alive and monitors their responses. These organoids are less than a millimeter across and lack several structures that a human brain has, but contain about 10,000 neurons, as well as supporting cells. The multielectrode arrays allow them to receive electrical signals.

First, the scientists applied a sensor that records tactile data to the 26 letters of the Braille alphabet. Then they converted this data to electrical stimulation patterns and presented the organoids with the different patterns to see if they would produce neural activity that could tell the scientists what stimulus they’d received. In other words, were they able to ‘read’ the electrical signal that corresponded to each Braille letter, and produce a signal that recognizably corresponded to the information they’d been given?

The organoids’ patterns of neural activity were classified using a simple machine learning algorithm, a support vector machine, that could sort the patterns and detect whether given signals corresponded to specific letters. A single organoid consistently produced a signal that could be accurately decoded as a letter about 61% of the time. However, three organoids working together produced a recognizable signal about 83% of the time.

“After processing by the organoids, the tactile data still contains enough information to classify Braille letters with good accuracy,” said Dr Benjamin Ward-Cherrier of Bristol University, senior author of the article. “Combining outputs from several organoids also showed an improvement in performance.”

The researchers can’t yet tell why three organoids performed better than just one; it could be because individual variation between the organoids means that they complement each other.

“Different organoids may have slightly different network connections, developmental states, and ongoing activity, so the same input can produce similar but not identical responses,” said Liu. “Combining those responses may give us complementary information that we would not get from a single organoid. At the same time, if every organoid behaves differently, it obviously makes it harder to build a predictable and standardized system.”

To make the task harder, the scientists applied different noise filters to the Braille letter signals. They also used the same support vector machine to compare decoding from the organoid responses with direct decoding of the deliberately obscured signals. The machine decoding directly, without the organoids’ involvement, turned out to be easier to fool than decoding from the organoid responses — it was less able to identify the letter signals among the artificial noise.

The scientists stress that these experiments don’t show if organoids can learn over time; they just show that the organoids received and responded to the Braille signals.

“We showed that tactile information could be encoded, processed through the organoids, and decoded, but we did not demonstrate learning or long-term changes in the organoids,” said Liu. “We also tested one tactile task using a fixed encoding scheme and a relatively simple measure of neural activity. The next step is definitely to move beyond Braille; we are interested in things such as textures, edges, and different kinds of touch, and eventually in closed-loop tasks where the organoid receives feedback from what it does. That would allow us to start asking whether the organoid can actually adapt through experience.”

REPUBLISHING GUIDELINES : Open access and sharing research is part of Frontiers’ mission . Unless otherwise noted, you can republish articles posted in the Frontiers news site — as long as you include a link back to the original research. Selling the articles is not allowed.
